votes for the transaction in its voting phase; a fully-voted transaction moves to prepared;
a prepared transaction commits, granting the downlink and setting the holder's belief; a
transaction is aborted; the holder gives the downlink back; a drone crashes silently; the
watchdog reclaims the downlink from a crashed holder; a crashed non-holder is recovered.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any drone that believes it holds the downlink is the drone the grant
record names, so two drones can never both believe they have the downlink and stream at
once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the downlink is granted, it eventually becomes ungranted again,
so the swarm never loses the downlink to a drone forever.

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    TotalCells = 3
    TankCap = 2
    QueueCap = 2
INVARIANT FuelCellsAreConserved
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm runs off a fixed stock of fuel cells trucked to the
staging field. Every cell is at any moment in exactly one place: racked in the field depot,
loaded in one of the two drones' tanks, or already burned on a sortie. Cells are not
manufactured and not thrown away, so the count of them cannot change.

Refuelling goes through a bounded request queue with backpressure: a drone that wants fuel
puts a request on the tail of the queue, and while the queue is full no further request is
accepted. The ground crew serves the request at the head of the queue, moving one cell out
of the depot rack into that drone's tank; it only does so if there is a cell in the rack and
room in that drone's tank. A request the crew cannot serve is dropped off the head of the
queue and the drone can ask again. A flying drone burns a cell from its tank on a sortie.

A drone can crash silently -- it goes down over the fire line without a mayday, and it may
go down with cells still in its tank. The recovery team walks out to a downed drone and
brings its cells back to the depot rack one at a time. A downed drone whose tank has been
emptied is trucked back and returned to the swarm.

Actions: a live drone puts a refuel request on the tail of the queue while the queue has
room; the ground crew serves the head request, moving a cell from the rack into that
drone's tank; the crew drops an unservable head request off the queue; a live drone burns a
cell from its tank; a drone crashes silently; the recovery team brings a cell back from a
downed drone's tank to the rack; an emptied downed drone is returned to the swarm.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The cells racked in the depot, plus the cells in the two drones' tanks,
plus the cells already burned always add up to the field's total fuel-cell stock, so no
refuel, sortie, crash or recovery ever creates or loses a cell.

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    TotalTokens = 3
    QueueCap = 2
INVARIANT TokensAreConserved
PROPERTY QueueAlwaysClears
nl:
A smart-home door lock network works from a fixed set of guest access tokens. Every token is
at any moment in exactly one place: sitting in the household vault, queued at the hub for
provisioning onto a particular lock, installed on a lock, or retired after being revoked.
Tokens are never minted and never destroyed; a retired token is recycled back into the
vault rather than thrown away.

Provisioning goes through the hub's bounded queue, which applies backpressure: while the
queue holds its full number of tokens nothing further is taken out of the vault, and each
lock has at most one token queued for it at a time. Queuing a token takes it out of the
vault; installing it puts it onto the lock it was queued for.

The radio to the locks reorders freely, so the hub does not work the queue in arrival
order: it installs whichever queued token it likes. A queued token can also be pulled back
into the vault instead of being installed.

Revoking a guest takes their token off its lock and retires it; recycling puts a retired
token back in the vault.

Actions: a token is taken from the vault and queued for a lock while the queue has room and
that lock has nothing queued; the hub installs a queued token onto its lock; the hub pulls a
queued token back into the vault; a guest's token is revoked off its lock and retired; a
retired token is recycled into the vault.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The tokens in the vault, plus the tokens queued at the hub, plus the
tokens installed on the front, back and side locks, plus the retired tokens always add up to
the household's total token count.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every token queued for a lock eventually leaves the queue, so nothing
sits queued at the hub forever.

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Operators = {opRed, opBlue}
    TotalUnits = 3
INVARIANT UnitsAreConserved
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch works with a fixed number of settlement units for the
day. Every unit is at any moment in exactly one place: unallocated in the batch pool,
earmarked against one of the nostro accounts, or already settled out. Units are neither
created nor written off during the batch; a returned settlement simply comes back into the
pool.

Earmarking is protected by two levels of lock, coarse before fine. A batch operator takes
the batch lock first, which covers the whole run, and only while holding it may it take the
lock on an individual nostro account. Both locks are held together until the operator drops
them in one step, releasing the batch lock and every account lock in its name. Only an
operator holding both the batch lock and a given account's lock may move a unit out of the
pool and earmark it against that account.

Settlement confirmations come back from the rail with no ordering guarantee whatsoever.
They arrive for whichever account the rail feels like, in whatever order, and they are
applied as they land: a confirmation moves one earmarked unit on that account out to
settled. Confirmations do not wait on locks and do not care which operator earmarked the
unit.

Actions: an operator takes the free batch lock; an operator holding the batch lock takes a
free account lock; an operator holding both moves a unit from the pool to an earmark on
that account; a confirmation lands and moves an earmarked unit out to settled; an operator
drops the batch lock and all of its account locks; a settlement is returned and its unit
comes back into the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The units left in the batch pool, plus the units earmarked against the two
nostro accounts, plus the units already settled always add up to the day's total settlement
units.

    /\ writing = {}

    /\ r \notin writing
    /\ Cardinality(waiting) < QueueCap

    /\ session = FreeChannel
    /\ r \in waiting
    /\ session' = r
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {r}

    /\ session = r
    /\ r \notin writing
    /\ writing' = writing \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, waiting, overrideOn>>

    /\ writing' = writing \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, waiting, overrideOn>>

    /\ r \notin writing
    /\ session' = FreeChannel
    /\ UNCHANGED <<writing, waiting, overrideOn>>

    /\ overrideOn' = FALSE

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    QueueCap = 2
INVARIANT WritersHoldTheSession
PROPERTY WritesAlwaysEnd
nl:
A smart-home door lock network programs its locks over a single radio channel. That channel
is the critical resource: only one requester may have a programming session on it, and only
a requester with the session may actually be writing to the locks.

Requesters queue for the channel. The queue is bounded and applies backpressure: while it
is full nothing more joins it, and a requester already holding the session or already
writing does not queue. The channel controller grants the session to a queued requester
whenever the channel is free. A requester with the session begins a write and ends it; it
may only hand the channel back once it has stopped writing.

The householder has a privileged override. Seizing the channel cuts every write dead and
frees the session in the same step, so nothing is left writing without a session, and while
the override is in force the controller grants the session to nobody. The householder
releases the override afterwards.

Actions: a requester joins the queue while the queue has room; the controller grants the
free channel to a queued requester while the override is not in force; a requester with the
session begins writing; a writing requester ends its write; a requester that is not writing
hands the channel back; the householder seizes the channel, cutting all writes and freeing
the session; the householder releases the override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every requester that is writing to the locks is a requester holding the
programming session, so two requesters can never be writing at once and nothing writes
without the session.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every write that begins eventually ends, so the channel is never left
with a write running forever.

    /\ unreported' = [unreported EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, reported, cartLease>>

ReportLands(p) ==
    /\ unreported[p] > 0
    /\ unreported' = [unreported EXCEPT ![p] = @ - 1]
    /\ reported' = reported + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, feeder, cartLease>>

PulpAndRack ==
    /\ reported > 0
    /\ reported' = reported - 1
    /\ store' = store + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeder, unreported, cartLease>>

Next ==
    \/ PulpAndRack
    \/ \E p \in Presses :
           \/ TakeCartLease(p) \/ LoadFromStore(p) \/ CountdownTicks(p) \/ LeaseLapses(p)
           \/ RenewLease(p) \/ PrintReam(p) \/ ReportLands(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ReamsAreConserved ==
    store + feeder["pressQuarto"] + feeder["pressFolio"]
        + unreported["pressQuarto"] + unreported["pressFolio"] + reported = TotalReams

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    TotalReams = 3
    LeaseLife = 2
INVARIANT ReamsAreConserved
nl:
A print shop job spooler works from a fixed number of paper reams for the run. Every ream is
at any moment in exactly one place: racked in the store room, loaded in one of the two
presses' feeders, printed but not yet reported, or printed and reported into the day's
total. Reams are neither delivered nor scrapped mid-run; reported reams are pulped and
racked back into the store room.

There is one paper cart, and it is handed out as a lease rather than a lock. A press takes
the cart lease only while no press holds it, and the lease carries a countdown that ticks
down on its own. A press still loading renews its lease, putting the countdown back to full;
if the countdown runs out the lease simply lapses and the cart is free for another press.
Only a press holding a live lease may move a ream out of the store room into its feeder.

A press prints a ream out of its feeder, which puts it into that press's unreported pile.
Completion reports come back from the presses over the shop network, which gives no
ordering guarantee: a report lands for whichever press, in whatever order, and moves one
ream from that press's unreported pile into the day's reported total.

Actions: a press takes the free cart lease; a press holding a live lease moves a ream from
the store room into its feeder; a lease countdown ticks down; a lease lapses when its
countdown runs out; a press renews its lease; a press prints a ream from its feeder into its
unreported pile; a completion report lands and moves a ream from a press's unreported pile
into the reported total; a reported ream is pulped back into the store room.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The reams racked in the store room, plus the reams in the two presses'
feeders, plus the reams in the two presses' unreported piles, plus the reams in the reported
total always add up to the run's total ream count.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m8p0t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

Crews == {"crewDawn", "crewDusk"}
Lanes == {"laneInner", "laneOuter"}
FreeLock == "freeLock"
Nobody == "nobody"
NoLane == "noLane"
ArchIdle == [crew |-> Nobody, lane |-> NoLane]

VARIABLES tunnelLock, laneLock, arch, inService

vars == <<tunnelLock, laneLock, arch, inService>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ tunnelLock \in Crews \cup {FreeLock}
    /\ laneLock \in [Lanes -> Crews \cup {FreeLock}]
    /\ arch \in [crew : Crews \cup {Nobody}, lane : Lanes \cup {NoLane}]
    /\ inService \subseteq Lanes

Init ==
    /\ tunnelLock = FreeLock
    /\ laneLock = [l \in Lanes |-> FreeLock]
    /\ arch = ArchIdle
    /\ inService = Lanes

TakeTunnelLock(k) ==
    /\ tunnelLock = FreeLock
    /\ tunnelLock' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<laneLock, arch, inService>>

TakeLaneLock(k, l) ==
    /\ tunnelLock = k
    /\ l \in inService
    /\ laneLock[l] = FreeLock
    /\ laneLock' = [laneLock EXCEPT ![l] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tunnelLock, arch, inService>>

MountArch(k, l) ==
    /\ tunnelLock = k
    /\ laneLock[l] = k
    /\ l \in inService
    /\ arch.crew = Nobody
    /\ arch' = [crew |-> k, lane |-> l]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tunnelLock, laneLock, inService>>

DismountArch(k) ==
    /\ arch.crew = k
    /\ arch' = ArchIdle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tunnelLock, laneLock, inService>>

DropLocks(k) ==
    /\ tunnelLock = k
    /\ arch.crew # k
    /\ tunnelLock' = FreeLock
    /\ laneLock' = [l \in Lanes |-> IF laneLock[l] = k THEN FreeLock ELSE laneLock[l]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<arch, inService>>

OpenLane(l) ==
    /\ l \notin inService
    /\ inService' = inService \cup {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tunnelLock, laneLock, arch>>

CloseLane(l) ==
    /\ l \in inService
    /\ laneLock[l] = FreeLock
    /\ arch.lane # l
    /\ inService' = inService \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tunnelLock, laneLock, arch>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Crews : TakeTunnelLock(k) \/ DismountArch(k) \/ DropLocks(k)
    \/ \E k \in Crews, l \in Lanes : TakeLaneLock(k, l) \/ MountArch(k, l)
    \/ \E l \in Lanes : OpenLane(l) \/ CloseLane(l)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(DismountArch("crewDawn"))
    /\ WF_vars(DismountArch("crewDusk"))

ArchCrewHoldsItsLane ==
    arch.crew # Nobody =>
        /\ laneLock[arch.lane] = arch.crew
        /\ arch.lane \in inService

ArchAlwaysFreesUp == (arch.crew # Nobody) ~> (arch.crew = Nobody)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ArchCrewHoldsItsLane
PROPERTY ArchAlwaysFreesUp
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line finishes cars under a single blower arch. The arch is the critical
resource: it can dry one lane at a time, and while it is running it records both the crew
that mounted it and the lane it is serving.

Access is taken through two levels of lock, coarse before fine. A crew takes the tunnel
lock, which covers the whole conveyor, and only while holding it may it take the lock on an
individual lane. The tunnel lock is not handed back early: a crew keeps it together with its
lane locks and drops the lot in one step at the end, and it may only drop them once it is
not the crew on the arch. A crew holding the tunnel lock and a lane's lock may mount the
arch on that lane if nobody is on it, and it dismounts when the lane is dry.

The number of lanes in service changes while the line runs, as lanes are opened for the
rush and closed for cleaning. A lane may only be closed while its lock is free and the arch
is not serving it, so closing a lane never pulls it out from under a crew or the arch. A
lane must be in service for a crew to lock it or to mount the arch on it.

Actions: a crew takes the free tunnel lock; a crew holding the tunnel lock takes the free
lock on an in-service lane; a crew holding both mounts the free arch on that lane; the crew
on the arch dismounts; a crew that is not on the arch drops the tunnel lock and all of its
lane locks; a lane is opened for service; an unlocked, unserved lane is closed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the blower arch is running, the crew named on it holds the lock on
the very lane the arch is serving and that lane is still in service, so two crews can never
be on the arch at once and the arch never runs on a lane its crew does not hold.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every crew that mounts the blower arch eventually dismounts it, so the
arch is never left occupied forever.
